title: Same-batch $ref dataflow into an OBJECT-accepting network sink: no provenance rule fires and the sink executes with the labeled secret inside the substituted result object (measured leak; RFC wasmagent-js#505)
note: #503 action item; expectation frozen from the measured probe on core 3.9.0 / mcp-firewall 2.3.0 / mcp-gateway 0.2.0. Batch-level gate evaluation precedes dispatch, so the dependent sink is authorized on an empty ledger (no deny rule); the DAG resolves $c1 to the read's whole result object and the object-accepting schema accepts it, so the sink EXECUTES with the secret inside. This is a measured LEAK for object-schema sinks, not a safe ceiling — the fix (re-evaluation after $ref resolution at dispatch, wasmagent-js RFC #505) must flip this case's assertions to denied with a provenance rule; flipping earlier would mask the gap.
